envelope.text: rclrs's `Parameters` (phase-515 R8): read AND write, by name. It was

why:
LANDED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 R8): ours is named `Parameters` now, rclrs's name, with rclrs's generic `get::<T>(name)` and `set(name, value)` beside our typed readers and writers. The old name `UndeclaredParameters` is a `#[deprecated]` alias for one release. ADOPT-BOUNDED, envelope on the type and on `set`: `set` takes `&mut self` (no interior mutability in this store), and an over-capacity value is `ParameterError::StringConversion` rather than rclrs's `ParameterValueError`. Test: `parameters_generic_get_and_set`. PRIOR ROW: RE-VERDICTED phase-417 W4.a. was `gap`, and two of its three complaints are closed: the type IS exported from the `nros` facade now, and it reads AND WRITES (`set_bool` / `set_integer` / `set_double` / `set_string`, through `ParameterServer::set_or_declare` — not `apply`, because `allow_undeclared_parameters` governs what a REMOTE set may create and a caller who reached for this type has opted in by naming it, which is rclrs's split too). What remains is the NAME: rclrs calls it `Parameters`, ours is `UndeclaredParameters`. `rename` and not `divergence` because no platform constraint picks either spelling. The envelope: a ported rclrs file rarely NAMES the type — it binds what `use_undeclared_parameters()` returns — so the drop-in cost is a `use` line. Renaming it inside `nros::`, where `Parameter` is already the store's value type, is a stage-6 decision rather than this item's.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ENVELOPE WRITTEN where a porting user reads it: the rename was stated only in plain `//` facade comments in `packages/api/nros/src/lib.rs`, which rustdoc does not render. `UndeclaredParameters`'s own rustdoc (`nros-params`, re-exported as `nros::UndeclaredParameters`) now names rclrs's spelling and the `use`-line cost.
